- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x prior high or adjust downward by 1–2% after spike.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model overestimates downward trend — reduce forecast slope or add slight upward bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates upside — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment > -0.10.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ days below 65), model often over-predicts decline — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and model forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid “sentiment mismatch”.
- If model forecast is below true outcome by >2% for 3+ days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 3–5 days.
